## Submission checklist

- goal and success criteria written before AI use;
- tool/model named and AI's limited job stated;
- prompt link or accessible export with private information removed;
- meaningful versions and decision notes;
- verified sources and licences;
- measurements, tests and observations made by the student;
- exact disclosure of what AI produced or changed;
- explanation of what the student accepted, rejected, revised and why.

## Example disclosure

> I used **[tool/model]** on **[date]** to generate three questions for evaluating my name-tag layout and to identify claims that needed checking. I verified the blank dimensions myself, rejected the suggested machine settings because they were not from our local procedure, and changed the spacing after a printed-size test. The logo, CAD model, fabrication decisions and final evaluation are my own work.

Follow the assignment and rubric first. Disclosure does not turn prohibited use into permitted use, and hidden AI use prevents the teacher from evaluating the student's actual learning.
